card.name: Sinte
card.era: Traditional; popularised in Conakry/global scene from mid-1990s
card.tagline: Nalu/Landuma celebration and pre-initiation dance of coastal Guinea
card.profile: Sinte (Sinte, Nalou Fate) is a rhythm and dance from the region of Boke and Boffa in coastal Guinea, used by the Landuma and Nalu (Nalou) peoples as a pre-initiation/celebration dance, sometimes linked to transformation after circumcision (Alpha Rhythm Roots; Tontinkan; Course Hero). Originally played on very large krin (hollow-log) drums - sometimes a single large krin played by three people in unison - it has been adapted to djembe and dunun and is celebrated for its melody and varied associated dances (Tontinkan; Wula Drum).
card.insight: Guinean master M'Bemba Bangoura created the ensemble djembe/dunun version after dancer Bangaly Bangoura brought the village dance to Conakry in 1996, recording it on his debut CD 'Wali'; it then spread widely especially via Youssouf Koumbassa (Wula Drum).
card.image_significance: The Baga coast's pre-initiation dance. A representative image shows drum-driven communal movement, often in a circle with vivid textiles — Boke/Boffa, Guinea.
